chunks: Title: AI Regulation in India (High-level Notes)

India is working on AI governance through frameworks, advisory documents, and broader digital regulation efforts.
Key themes include:
1) Responsible AI: fairness, transparency, accountability, and explainability.
2) Data privacy: how AI systems collect, process, and store user data.
3) Risk-based governance: stricter rules for high-risk systems (healthcare, finance, public services).
4) Deepfakes and misinformation: proposals often discuss labeling, detection, and penalties.

4) Deepfakes and misinformation: proposals often discuss labeling, detection, and penalties.
5) Public sector adoption: AI in healthcare, agriculture, and education needs safety and reliability.

Common challenges:
- Fast tech growth vs slow legal changes
- Bias and discrimination risks
- Lack of high-quality public datasets
- Compute cost and infrastructure gaps
- Skill gap in AI governance

Conclusion:
India’s AI regulation is evolving, focusing on safety + innovation balance.

Title: Internal Policy - AI Assistant Guidelines

The assistant must follow:
1) Do not give medical diagnosis as final truth; always provide disclaimer.
2) Provide citations when possible.
3) If the user asks for legal/medical advice, respond carefully.
4) If confidence is low, ask clarifying questions.
5) Avoid hallucinating facts, numbers, and laws.

The assistant should produce:
- short answer
- detailed answer
- key bullet points
- "sources used" section (document name or chunk reference)

Title: FAQs

Q: What is RAG?
A: Retrieval-Augmented Generation. It retrieves relevant chunks from documents and then generates an answer.

Q: Why embeddings?
A: Embeddings convert text into vectors so we can search semantically.

Q: What is a vector database?
A: A storage system for embeddings that supports similarity search.

Q: What is chunking?
A: Splitting text into smaller pieces to store and retrieve efficiently.
Title: LangGraph Quick Notes

LangGraph is used to build agent workflows with explicit state and graph-based orchestration.
Key concepts:
- State: a dictionary-like object shared across nodes.
- Nodes: functions that read state and return partial updates.
- Edges: define execution flow from node to node.
- Conditional edges: routing decisions based on state.
- Persistence / Checkpointer: saves state at each step for fault tolerance, resume, and time travel debugging.
- Threads: separate conversation runs using thread_id.

Why LangGraph:
- easy loops and iterations
- better control for multi-step agents
- can combine multiple tools and decisions cleanly

Title: Diabetes ML Notes

Diabetes prediction datasets often contain features like glucose level, BMI, age, pregnancies, insulin, and blood pressure.
Model flow:
1) Data cleaning
2) Train-test split
3) Model training (Logistic Regression / RandomForest / XGBoost)
4) Evaluate using accuracy and ROC-AUC
5) Predict probability using predict_proba

Important:
- Dataset may contain zero values for medical measures (glucose=0 etc), which can represent missing values.
- Probability threshold usually 0.5 but can be tuned.

this basic idea. They also attempt to discourage rote learning and the maintenance of sharp

PREFACE
It gives me pleasure to place this book in the hands of the students, teachers and the public at
large (whose role cannot be overlooked). It is a natural sequel to the Class XI textbook which
was brought out in 2006. This book is also a trimmed version of the textbooks which existed so
far. The chapter on thermal and chemical effects of current has been cut out. This topic has also
been dropped from the CBSE syllabus. Similarly, the chapter on communications has been

been dropped from the CBSE syllabus. Similarly, the chapter on communications has been
substantially curtailed. It has been rewritten in an easily comprehensible form.
Although most other chapters have been based on the earlier versions, several parts and
sections in them have been rewritten. The Development Team has been guided by the feedback
received from innumerable teachers across the country.
In producing these books, Class XI as well as Class XII, there has been a basic change of

In producing these books, Class XI as well as Class XII, there has been a basic change of
emphasis. Both the books present physics to students without assuming that they would pursue
this subject beyond the higher secondary level. This new view has been prompted by the various
observations and suggestions made in the National Curriculum Framework (NCF), 2005.
Similarly, in today’s educational scenario where students can opt for various combinations of

Similarly, in today’s educational scenario where students can opt for various combinations of
subjects, we cannot assume that a physics student is also studying mathematics. Therefore,
physics has to be presented, so to say, in a standalone form.
As in Class XI textbook, some interesting box items have been inserted in many chapters.
They are not meant for teaching or examinations. Their purpose is to catch the attention of the

reader, to show some applications in daily life or in other areas of science and technology, to
suggest a simple experiment, to show connection of concepts in different areas of physics, and
in general, to break the monotony and enliven the book.

almost always that the question ‘why’ has no answer within the domain of physics and science
in general. But that itself is a learning experience, is it not? On the other hand, the question
‘how’ has been reasonably well answered by physicists in the case of most natural phenomena.

ITER is a joint international research and development project that
aims to demonstrate the scientific and technical feasibility of fusion power.

India is one of the seven full partners in the project, the others being
the European Union (represented by EURATOM), Japan, the People’s
Republic of China, the Republic of Korea, the Russian Federation and the
USA. ITER will be constructed in Europe, at Cadarache in the South of
France and will provide 500 MW of fusion power.

abundant fuel resources, to meet the needs of a growing world population.
